noClients: No client registered a command_endpoint. It is a registration member (RFC 7591, POST /oauth2/register) and a field on /admin/applications.
noAccounts: No relying party has reported an account yet.
note: OpenID Provider Commands 1.0. This service tells a relying party what to do with an account — a signed Command Token POSTed to the command_endpoint it registered. Provider commands are {enabled, select, on {on} other {off}} here (oauth2.providerCommands); automatic commands on a disable, an enable, a delete, a change and a global sign-out are {automatic, select, on {on} other {off}} (oauth2.commandAutomatic) and go only to a relying party whose metadata answer listed the command. The issuer Command Tokens name is
accountsHeading: Accounts, as each relying party reported them
deliveriesNote: Every outbound delivery this service POSTs to an address a client registered, on the one durable queue: each is a persisted row, attempted once for the cluster under a claimed lease, retried with backoff when a timeout, a connection failure, 5xx, 408 or 429 makes that worth it, and a dead letter otherwise — sent again only when an operator presses Retry, which starts a new generation.
